definition: The failure mode where models spend long reasoning chains on easy queries, adding cost and sometimes talking themselves out of correct answers.
details: The failure mode where models spend long reasoning chains on easy queries, adding cost and sometimes talking themselves out of correct answers. Motivates adaptive thinking budgets, difficulty-aware routing, and training objectives that penalize wasted deliberation.

explainer.lead: Overthinking is the failure mode where models spend long reasoning chains on easy queries, adding cost and sometimes talking themselves out of correct answers. It motivates adaptive thinking budgets and difficulty-aware routing.

tiers.eli5: It is like writing a three-page essay to answer whether today is Tuesday, and talking yourself into the wrong day along the way.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers counter it with adaptive thinking budgets, difficulty-aware routing, and training objectives that penalize wasted deliberation. A pitfall is capping reasoning too aggressively and losing accuracy on genuinely hard queries.
tiers.paperLevel: Overthinking is defined as excessive reasoning-chain length on easy queries that raises cost and can reduce correctness; mitigations are adaptive budgets, routing, and penalized-deliberation objectives.

explainer.example: A model spends thousands of reasoning tokens on a simple arithmetic question and, after second-guessing, outputs a wrong sum.
